title: Nineveh · Trace the record
question: A post quotes a line from the Flood Tablet. What do you record first?

choices.label: The tablet’s collection record, object number, and the translation used
The social media post as the tablet’s original wording

feedback: Start with British Museum object K.3375. Record the translator and edition separately whenever you quote a translation.

title: Dewey and LCC · Follow the index
question: Two catalogs use different class labels for a work. Which step lets you check whether the records refer to the same edition?

choices.label: Treat the label that appears first as the edition identifier
Compare the author, title, publication details, and identifiers

feedback: Classification helps you find a record. Edition details help you verify which text it describes.

source.label: Library of Congress · Classification and Shelflisting

title: Everything and Nothing · Keep the record intact
question: The Library of Congress row reads 1 - 1 = 2. Prompt 1 gives both operating equations. How do you record this?

choices.label: Keep the row verbatim and link a note recording Prompt 1’s equations

feedback: The original line remains available for inspection. Prompt 1 supplies 1 + 1 = 2 for Everything and 1 - 1 = 0 for Nothing.

title: Protecting The One · Choose the audience
question: A family account is useful to a lesson and includes a private detail. What goes into the public index?

choices.label: The entire record, with the private detail included
Only the details cleared for publication, with the original kept within its authorized audience

feedback: Preserve the original under its access rules. Confirm that the description and its metadata are cleared before release.
